title: Massachusetts Democrats Vote in Senate Primary on August 31, 2026
dek: Massachusetts Democrats voted on August 31, 2026, to choose their Senate nominee between incumbent Senator Ed Markey, 80, and U.S. Representative Seth Moulton, 48. Markey is backed by prominent progressives including Elizabeth Warren and Bernie Sanders; Moulton has support from The Boston Globe and several House colleagues.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: Markey, the second-oldest sitting U.S. senator seeking reelection, has the endorsement of U.S. Senators Elizabeth Warren and Bernie Sanders and U.S. Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, while his challenger Moulton received backing from The Boston Globe and current and former House colleagues.
bottom_line: As of Thursday, August 29, approximately 468,000 ballots had already been cast early or by mail in Tuesday's election, including roughly 390,000 from Democrats and 78,000 from Republicans. Final results determine the Democratic nominee for the general election in November 2026.
body: Massachusetts Democrats voted on August 31, 2026, to select their Democratic Senate nominee in a primary matchup between U.S. Senator Ed Markey, who turned 80 in July 2026, and U.S. Representative Seth Moulton, a six-term congressman who will turn 48 in October 2026.

Markey has served in the Senate since 2013 after holding a House seat for nearly 37 years. Moulton briefly sought the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination. In his last competitive primary in 2020, Markey defeated then-U.S. Representative Joseph Kennedy III, 55 percent to 45 percent.

Markey is described by the Associated Press as the second-oldest sitting U.S. senator seeking reelection in 2026. His backers include U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont, and U.S. Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York. A majority of delegates to the state party convention in May voted to endorse Markey, though Moulton won enough support to qualify for the primary ballot.

Moulton has endorsements from The Boston Globe and from current and former Democratic House colleagues, including New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill. Over the course of the campaign, Markey raised and spent more than 8 million dollars compared with more than 6 million dollars for Moulton, according to available filings. As of August 12, Moulton held a slight advantage in cash-on-hand over Markey.

Essex County, which includes Moulton's hometown of Salem and falls within his 6th Congressional District, emerged as a potential battleground. Markey swept all four major counties, Suffolk, Middlesex, Essex, and Norfolk, in his 2020 primary victory over Kennedy. He beat Kennedy in Essex County by a 9-point margin that year.

A separate six-way Democratic primary is underway in the 6th Congressional District to succeed Moulton. That race includes former Andover Selectman Dan Koh, who has endorsements from former President Joe Biden and former Vice President Kamala Harris; financial technology executive John Beccia; and state Representative Tram Nguyen, who is backed by U.S. Representative Lori Trahan. Koh previously served in the Biden White House and was a top aide to Marty Walsh during his tenures as Boston mayor and U.S. secretary of labor. Koh narrowly lost the 2018 primary for the neighboring 3rd Congressional District to Trahan. In fundraising, Koh raised about 4.7 million dollars in contributions, Nguyen raised about 895,000 dollars, and Beccia loaned his campaign 4 million dollars.

In the 8th Congressional District, 13-term Democratic U.S. Representative Stephen Lynch faced a primary challenge from attorney Patrick Roath, who outraised the incumbent. Republican Micah Q. Jones ran unopposed for the Republican nomination in the 6th Congressional District.
